explainer_reply:
Looking at the activations, the dominant pattern is periods at the end of sentences (appearing in the majority of examples), followed by newlines marking paragraph or line breaks (in prose, code, and poetry), commas, and connective function words like "and," "so," "now," "by," "that," and "till." The sentence-initial words ("So," "And," "Now") also appear right at the start of new sentences. What unifies these is that they all occur at structural transition points in text — where one sentence, clause, or paragraph ends and another begins.

[EXPLANATION]: Tokens at structural boundaries between sentences, clauses, or paragraphs — primarily sentence-ending periods, paragraph-breaking newlines, and connective words (and, so, now, by, that) that mark discourse transitions.
